title: Power Apps: modern responsive template for canvas apps created from SharePoint lists
summary: The briefing's roadmap facts, template behaviour and general licensing and billing statements are supported. Two minor corrections remain: extend the data policy path to connector classification, and replace the unnecessary uncertainty about data policy coverage with its documented scope.

claims.claim: The roadmap product is Power Apps.
claims.quote: "products": ["Power Apps"]

claims.claim: Microsoft plans an updated SharePoint/Microsoft Lists app-from-data experience for makers.
claims.quote: the updated SharePoint/Microsoft Lists app-from-data experience gives makers responsive record browsing

claims.where: What's changing; Why it matters; Risk assessment; rationale: risk
claims.claim: The generated app is a standalone canvas app, not an embedded SharePoint customised form.
claims.quote: It creates a standalone canvas app, not an embedded SharePoint customized form.

claims.claim: The updated experience provides responsive record browsing with grid and list views.
claims.quote: responsive record browsing with grid and list views

claims.claim: The updated experience provides separate screens for creating and editing records.
claims.quote: plus separate screens for creating and editing records.

claims.claim: The roadmap status is In development.
claims.quote: "status": "In development"

claims.where: front matter: targetDate; What's changing; Open questions
claims.claim: The roadmap target is February CY2027, described as a target rather than a commitment.
claims.quote: "targetDate": "February CY2027"

claims.claim: The roadmap preview target is November CY2026.
claims.quote: "previewDate": "November CY2026"

claims.where: front matter: clouds; What's changing; Scope
claims.claim: The roadmap lists Worldwide (Standard Multi-Tenant) and no other clouds, without establishing exclusion elsewhere.
claims.quote: "clouds": ["Worldwide (Standard Multi-Tenant)"]

claims.where: front matter: platforms; What's changing; Scope
claims.claim: The roadmap platform is Web.
claims.quote: "platforms": ["Web"]

claims.claim: The roadmap lists both General Availability and Preview release phases.
claims.quote: "releasePhase": ["General Availability", "Preview"]

claims.claim: The roadmap describes public preview in early-release environments.
claims.quote: During public preview in early-release environments

claims.where: Why it matters; Governance guidance; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Connector and formula delegation limits still apply.
claims.quote: Connector and formula delegation limits still apply.

claims.claim: The updated template uses responsive containers.
claims.quote: The updated template uses responsive containers, a modern Data Grid, and modern forms.

claims.claim: The updated template uses a modern Data Grid.
claims.quote: The updated template uses responsive containers, a modern Data Grid, and modern forms.

claims.claim: The updated template uses modern forms.
claims.quote: The updated template uses responsive containers, a modern Data Grid, and modern forms.

claims.claim: The generated layout depends on the template available in the maker's environment.
claims.quote: The layout depends on the template available in your environment.

claims.claim: Learn also describes a responsive single-screen template combining browsing and record editing.
claims.quote: The responsive single-screen template combines browsing and record editing on one screen.

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; What's changing; Why it matters; Open questions
claims.claim: Microsoft has not stated which template a given environment receives by default or what happens on arrival.
claims.quote: Searched: SharePoint updated modern-controls app-from-data template disable enable admin default environment rollout; read app-from-sharepoint and roadmap. Neither specifies the default template or automatic replacement behaviour.

claims.claim: Microsoft has not specified the environment-by-environment distribution schedule beyond the roadmap targets.
claims.quote: Searched: SharePoint updated modern-controls app-from-data template disable enable admin default environment rollout; read app-from-sharepoint and roadmap. Only template availability by environment and the roadmap targets are given.

claims.claim: No source states that existing generated apps change with this template update.
claims.quote: Searched: Power Apps SharePoint updated app template existing apps permissions identity autonomous; read app-from-sharepoint and roadmap. Both describe generating apps, not updating existing apps.

claims.claim: A view switch on the records screen selects grid or list.
claims.quote: Use the view switch on the records screen to choose a grid or a list

claims.claim: Grid view displays records in columns.
claims.quote: Grid | Review records in columns and select rows.

claims.claim: The grid edit action appears when exactly one row is selected.
claims.quote: The edit action appears when you select exactly one row.

claims.claim: List view is a compact list from which users open item details.
claims.quote: List | Review a compact list and open an item to view its details.

claims.claim: The new-record form uses one column below an app width of 768.
claims.quote: The new-record form uses one column below an app width of 768 and two columns at widths of 768 or greater.

claims.claim: The new-record form uses two columns at an app width of 768 or greater.
claims.quote: The new-record form uses one column below an app width of 768 and two columns at widths of 768 or greater.

claims.claim: The cited Learn article does not mark itself as preview.
claims.quote: Searched: preview in the complete fetched Create a canvas app with data from a list article. Preview appears as an app-testing action, not as a feature preview designation.

claims.claim: Generated counts and collection-backed results do not guarantee that all records in a large list are loaded.
claims.quote: Generated counts and collection-backed results don't guarantee that every record in a large list is loaded.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Why it matters
claims.claim: The generated app connects to the list selected by the maker.
claims.quote: Select a list or select the sample list you created earlier, and then select Create app.

claims.claim: Adding or editing information in the app updates the source list.
claims.quote: When you add or edit information in the app, the information in SharePoint or Lists also updates.

claims.claim: Data-source permissions and connection access, rather than the template itself, govern access to the underlying data.
claims.quote: For a shared app to function as you expect, you must also manage permissions for the data source or sources on which the app is based

claims.claim: Grid view filters a generated collection.
claims.quote: Grid view filters a generated collection, while list view filters the connected data source.

claims.claim: List view filters the connected data source.
claims.quote: Grid view filters a generated collection, while list view filters the connected data source.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance guidance
claims.claim: The two views can return different records for the same filter on large lists.
claims.quote: Grid view filters a generated collection, while list view filters the connected data source. Check the same filter in both views after you connect your list. Generated counts and collection-backed results don't guarantee that every record in a large list is loaded.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Microsoft advises checking the same filter in both views.
claims.quote: Check the same filter in both views after you connect your list.

claims.claim: No new identity or permission model is described for this template.
claims.quote: Searched: Power Apps SharePoint updated app template existing apps permissions identity autonomous; read app-from-sharepoint, share-app, and connectors authentication search excerpts. No template-specific identity or permissions model is described.

claims.claim: The generated canvas app uses normal Power Apps sharing.
claims.quote: After you create an app, you can play, save, share, and publish it.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance controls
claims.claim: Assigning SharePoint to Business prevents combining it with connectors in Non-business or Blocked groups within the policy scope.
claims.quote: By moving the Salesforce and SharePoint connectors to the Business data group, you're preventing users from creating flows and apps that combine these two connectors with any of the connectors in the Non-business or Blocked groups.

claims.claim: Data policies are general connector controls, but the row says Microsoft has not confirmed their application to this template specifically.
claims.quote: After this policy is saved, any Power Apps or Power Automate maker, who is part of the data policy's environment, can create an app or a flow that shares data between SharePoint or Salesforce.
claims.fix: Replace the row note in front matter and the rendered table with: 'Applies to Power Apps apps in the environments covered by the policy. Governs connector combinations, not template availability.' The cited page states that scope without excluding generated canvas apps.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance controls
claims.claim: Microsoft has not described different data policy treatment for this template.
claims.quote: Searched: SharePoint template data policies canvas; read app-from-sharepoint and prevent-data-loss. Neither describes a template-specific exception to the general Power Apps policy scope.

claims.claim: The template documentation describes no autonomous or agent behaviour.
claims.quote: Searched: Power Apps SharePoint updated app template existing apps permissions identity autonomous; read app-from-sharepoint and roadmap. Described actions are interactive browsing and form actions, not autonomous execution.

claims.claim: Users create or edit records through the generated form screens.
claims.quote: Use the new-record action to open the form screen for a new item. Use a list item or the grid's edit action to open an existing record.

claims.claim: The form's save action calls SubmitForm.
claims.quote: Its save action calls SubmitForm on the generated form.

claims.claim: The form's OnFailure action shows an error notification.
claims.quote: Its OnFailure action shows an error notification.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Microsoft advises preserving the generated DataSource, Item, navigation formulas and form success and failure actions unless intentionally replacing their behaviour.
claims.quote: When you customize these screens, preserve the generated DataSource, Item, navigation formulas, and form success and failure actions unless you intentionally replace their behavior.

claims.claim: Generated control and screen names can vary, so names from older tutorials may not match.
claims.quote: The generated control and screen names can vary, so use the names in your app rather than names from an older tutorial.

claims.claim: Learn links separate SharePoint forms integration guidance for the embedded customised-form experience.
claims.quote: It isn't the same as a customized list form hosted inside SharePoint. For that experience, see Understand SharePoint forms integration.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: Microsoft has not published template-specific licensing terms.
claims.quote: Searched: SharePoint modern responsive canvas app template licensing price meter subscription; SharePoint template licensing Power Apps modern. Read app-from-sharepoint, powerapps-licensing-faq and pricing-billing-skus; no separate template terms are stated.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: Building canvas apps does not require a licence.
claims.quote: You don't need a license to build canvas apps. You need a license to build model-driven apps.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: Running apps requires appropriate entitlements.
claims.quote: Power Apps requires users to have an appropriate license to run apps

claims.claim: Some Microsoft 365 licences include limited Power Apps rights for Microsoft 365 data and standard connectors.
claims.quote: Some Microsoft 365 licenses include limited Power Apps and Power Automate use rights. These use rights are intended for scenarios that use Microsoft 365 data and standard connectors.

claims.claim: Premium capabilities can require additional entitlements.
claims.quote: Some examples of features that require premium entitlements include: premium connectors, Dataverse entities, on-premises data gateways, custom APIs, etc.

claims.claim: Managed Environments can require additional entitlements even for standard apps.
claims.quote: When you activate managed environments in an environment, all active usage requires a qualifying license as detailed in managed environments licensing. This requirement includes users who run standard apps

claims.claim: The feature article's prerequisite names subscriptions to Microsoft 365 and Microsoft Power Platform, without specifying a plan.
claims.quote: Use SharePoint and Power Apps with a subscription to Microsoft 365 and Microsoft Power Platform.

claims.claim: Mixed describes the general Power Apps entitlement options applicable to these canvas apps.
claims.quote: Microsoft Power Platform capabilities can be licensed through standalone licenses, use rights included with other Microsoft products, capacity add-ons, or pay-as-you-go meters.

claims.claim: Microsoft documents no separate template-specific meter.
claims.quote: Searched: SharePoint modern responsive canvas app template licensing price meter subscription; read app-from-sharepoint, pricing-billing-skus and the Power Apps section of pay-as-you-go-meters. No template-specific meter is stated.

claims.claim: The general Power Apps per-app meter can cover generated canvas apps where Power Apps pay-as-you-go is enabled.
claims.quote: The Power Apps per-app meter provides access to both canvas, and model-driven apps for authenticated users.

claims.where: front matter: cost; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: The applicable Power Apps per-app pay-as-you-go rate is $10 per active user/app/month, supporting the variable cost rating.
claims.quote: Power Apps per-app | The total number of unique monthly active users of each app in a pay-as-you-go environment. ... | $10 per active user/app/month

claims.claim: Pay-as-you-go usage is billed through the linked Azure subscription.
claims.quote: When you choose to use pay-as-you-go, Azure meters bill your Azure subscription for your usage of Power Platform services.

claims.claim: Users with Power Apps per-user licences are not counted in the per-app meter.
claims.quote: If a user has a Power Apps per-user license, the user isn't counted in the meter.

claims.claim: Users with qualifying Microsoft 365 Power Apps rights using standard-connector apps are not counted in the per-app meter.
claims.quote: If a user has a Microsoft 365 license, which provides access to Power Apps and is using an app with standard connectors, the user is also not counted in the meter.

claims.claim: The roadmap record states no licensing requirement.
claims.quote: During public preview in early-release environments, the updated SharePoint/Microsoft Lists app-from-data experience gives makers responsive record browsing with grid and list views, plus separate screens for creating and editing records.

claims.claim: Makers can start the list-connected app in Power Apps through Start with data > SharePoint.
claims.quote: From the home screen, select Start with data. On the Create an app page, select SharePoint.

claims.claim: From a SharePoint or Lists list, makers can use Integrate > Power Apps > Create an app.
claims.quote: Open a list in either SharePoint or Lists. ... Select Integrate > Power Apps > Create an app.

claims.claim: Power Platform admin center > Security > Settings > Data and privacy > Data policy reaches the data policy list.
claims.quote: Select Security in the navigation pane. ... under Settings, select Data and privacy. ... select the Data policy section. Select + New Policy.
claims.fix: The path reaches the correct list but stops before classification. Extend controls[0].ui.path and the rendered path to 'Security > Settings > Data and privacy > Data policy > + New Policy > Pre-built connectors > SharePoint > Move to Business' for the cited walkthrough.

claims.claim: New-DlpPolicy -NewPolicy $NewPolicy creates a data policy from the supplied policy object using Microsoft.PowerApps.Administration.PowerShell.
claims.quote:
New-DlpPolicy -NewPolicy $NewPolicy
Creates a new policy with the $NewPolicy object.

claims.where: controls[1]; summary; Governance controls; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Microsoft documents no tenant or environment UI switch or automation operation specifically enabling or disabling the updated template.
claims.quote: Searched: Power Apps SharePoint responsive template availability PowerShell Set-AdminPowerAppEnvironment pac admin Power Platform API setting. Read app-from-sharepoint and Learn excerpts for powerapps-powershell, pac admin and pac power-apps.

claims.claim: Get-DlpPolicy retrieves existing data policy objects.
claims.quote: The Get-DlpPolicy cmdlet retrieves policy objects for the logged in admin's tenant.

claims.where: Cost and licensing; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: Learn's pre-sharing checks include previewing both views at narrow and wide widths, comparing filters, and creating and editing a test record.
claims.quote: Preview both grid and list views at narrow and wide widths. ... Apply a filter and check that both views show the expected records. ... Create a test record, save it, and confirm the values in the source list. ... Open that record, edit it, and confirm the changes in the source list.
